step-1.text: Flip both tops onto something soft, underside up, and butt them together into the L shape.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 main desk top and 1 return top.

step-2.text: Screw the joining plates across the seam where the two tops meet. Check the edges are flush before you drive the last screw. The return goes on the left here, but it can go either way.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 joining plate and 8 screws.

step-3.text: Lay the L-shaped frame along both tops and screw it down through the pre-drilled holes. The frame is what ties the L together, so use every screw.

count-3.text: This step uses 2 frame beams and 12 screws.

step-4.text: Set one lifting column on the far end of the main top and one at the end of the return, cables toward the back, and bolt each one down.

count-4.text: This step uses 2 lifting columns and 8 bolts.

step-5.text: Bolt a foot across the end of each column. On the return the foot runs across it, so the desk stands steady both ways.

count-5.text: This step uses 2 foots and 8 bolts.

step-6.text: Screw the control box under the back of the main top and the keypad under the front edge. Plug both motor cables and the keypad into the box, then clip the cables up out of the way.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 control box, 1 keypad and 6 screws.

step-7.text: With a helper, lift the whole desk and turn it onto its feet. Lift it clear of the floor, do not pivot it on one leg.

count-7.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-8.text: Plug it in and run the first-time reset from your manual, usually holding the down button until the desk bottoms out. Then try up and down with nothing on top, and watch both columns move together.

count-8.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

done.text: Done. Your ARK PRO L l-shaped standing desk 63" is built. Give it a proud little pat.
